2. WHY YOU ARE RECEIVING THIS NOW

The Privacy Act's employee records exemption is narrower than most people assume. It applies to records about a current or former employee, held in relation to the employment relationship. It does not cover an applicant, and it does not cover a contractor. Much of what we collect during recruitment and onboarding is therefore collected as an applicant's information, under the full weight of the Australian Privacy Principles — so you get this notice first, before you hand anything over.

3. WHAT WE COLLECT

3.1 Identity and contact. Legal name, any previous names, date of birth, address, phone number, email address, and emergency contact details.

3.2 Work rights and identity evidence. Passport, visa, birth certificate, driver licence or other documents used to verify your identity and your right to work in Australia.

3.3 Professional. AHPRA registration details and conditions, qualifications, professional indemnity insurance, referee comments, CPD records, and where the role requires them, a Working with Children Check, NDIS Worker Screening Check or National Police Check.

3.4 Payroll and tax. Bank account details, tax file number declaration information, superannuation fund details, and salary or wage records.

3.5 Health, only where relevant. Pre-existing injuries relevant to the inherent requirements of the role, workplace injury and rehabilitation information, immunisation status where a role requires it, and information supporting a request for a workplace adjustment.

3.6 Employment records. Contract, position description, performance and supervision records, leave, training and any disciplinary matters.

4. HOW WE COLLECT IT

Usually from you directly — through this portal, forms, interviews and conversations. We may also collect from: referees you nominate; AHPRA's public register; the screening agency that issues a check you have applied for; the ATO, in relation to superannuation; a recruitment agency, if one introduced you; and a previous employer where you have consented to that contact.

5. WHY WE COLLECT IT, AND ON WHAT AUTHORITY

• To assess your application and decide whether to make an offer.
• To create and administer your employment — pay you, pay your superannuation, manage leave, and meet our record-keeping obligations under the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth).
• To meet tax and superannuation obligations. Providing a tax file number is not compulsory, but tax may be withheld at a higher rate if you do not, and the collection and handling of a TFN is separately regulated.
• To verify that you are legally entitled to work in Australia.
• To verify professional registration, screening and insurance where the role requires them, and to keep verifying them while you work here.
• To meet our work health and safety duties, and to manage a workplace injury claim.
• To meet obligations relating to the delivery of NDIS supports.

6. IF YOU DO NOT PROVIDE IT

You do not have to give us anything. But some of it we cannot work around: without identity and work-rights evidence we cannot lawfully employ you; without bank and superannuation details we cannot pay you correctly; without current registration and any screening the role requires, you cannot be rostered to participant-facing work. Where the information is optional, we will say so on the form.

7. WHO WE DISCLOSE IT TO

• Our payroll and accounting providers, and the ATO.
• Your nominated superannuation fund, or the ATO where we must request a stapled fund.
• Our insurers, including the workers compensation insurer, in relation to a claim.
• Screening agencies and AHPRA, to verify a check or a registration.
• Our IT and cloud service providers, who host the portal and our email under contract.
• A regulator, court or law enforcement agency where we are required or authorised by law.
• A professional adviser, such as a lawyer or accountant, where necessary.

Some of these providers store information outside Australia. Current arrangements: [TO CONFIRM: overseas storage locations and providers, or "all data is stored in Australia" if that is accurate].

We do not sell your information, and we do not use it for marketing.

8. HOW IT IS PROTECTED

Held in access-controlled systems, with the most sensitive fields — bank details, tax file numbers, identity document numbers — encrypted, masked in the interface, and visible only to the small number of people whose role requires them. Access is logged. Paper records are stored securely and disposed of by secure destruction.

9. HOW LONG WE KEEP IT

Employee records are kept for at least seven years after employment ends, as the Fair Work Act requires. Some categories are kept longer where another law requires it. Unsuccessful applicants' information is kept for [TO CONFIRM: retention period for unsuccessful applicants] and then destroyed.

10. ACCESS, CORRECTION AND COMPLAINTS

You can ask to see the personal information we hold about you, and ask us to correct it. Contact privacy@opaltherapy.com.au. We will respond within [TO CONFIRM: response timeframe in days].

If you are unhappy with how we have handled your information, tell us first — we would rather fix it. If you are not satisfied with our response, you can complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner at oaic.gov.au or 1300 363 992.

summary: The first page a new starter reads — what Opal Therapy is, what the first weeks look like, what to do before day one, and where to find everything else.
body:
WELCOME TO OPAL THERAPY

Welcome. We are glad you said yes.

You have joined a small occupational therapy practice, and small is the point rather than a stage we are trying to grow out of. It means the person who assessed a participant is usually the person who writes their report and the person who follows through on it. It means you will know every participant on your caseload by name. It also means your work is visible, and that what you decide to do on a Tuesday afternoon in someone's kitchen matters to the whole practice.

WHAT WE DO

We provide occupational therapy to people living with disability, most of it funded through the NDIS, and most of it delivered where people actually live — homes, schools, workplaces and community settings, including regional visits. Assessment, therapy, equipment and assistive technology, home modifications, functional capacity reporting, and the reports that unlock the funding a person needs.

WHAT WE CARE ABOUT

The participant decides. We bring expertise; we do not bring a plan for someone's life. Choice and control are not a slogan borrowed from the NDIS — they are the difference between therapy that is used and therapy that is politely tolerated.

Write it down properly. A clinical record is how a participant's story survives a change of therapist. It is also the only evidence that the work happened.

Say the awkward thing early. A concern raised on the day is a conversation. The same concern raised in three months is an incident.

Nobody is expected to know everything. Asking is a professional strength here, and supervision exists for exactly this.

YOUR FIRST WEEKS

Before you start, your onboarding checklist in the portal lists everything we need from you — identity and work rights, bank and superannuation details, your AHPRA registration, any screening checks your role requires, and the policies you will be asked to read and acknowledge. Your exact role, start date, manager and onboarding contact are shown at the top of that checklist, because they are specific to you rather than to this page.

Week one is mostly orientation: systems, the portal, the policies, meeting the team, and shadowing rather than carrying a caseload. Week two usually adds joint visits. You will pick up your own caseload when your supervisor thinks you are ready, not on a date decided in advance.

You will have supervision from the beginning, and more of it early on than later.

BEFORE DAY ONE — THREE THINGS

1. Complete your onboarding checklist in the portal. Some items — screening checks in particular — take weeks to come back, so start those first.
2. Read the Employee Handbook and the Tier 1 policies. You will be asked to acknowledge several of them.
3. Tell us anything we need to know to set you up well: an adjustment you need, a name or pronoun you go by that differs from your legal name, dietary requirements, or a date you already have booked.

IF SOMETHING GOES WRONG BEFORE YOU EVEN START

Contact [TO CONFIRM: onboarding contact name, role, email and phone]. A delayed check, a document you cannot find, a start date that no longer works — all of it is easier to solve before day one than after.

WHERE EVERYTHING LIVES

The portal holds your onboarding checklist, the policy library, your calendar, participant records and clinical documentation. The Employee Handbook explains how we work day to day. Every policy referenced anywhere is in the portal's document library, in full, at the version you acknowledged.

Welcome aboard.
